sections.html: Psalidodon balbus is a small characid known only from upper Paraná basin headwaters in the Federal District and Goiás, central Brazil. Most records come from the rio São Bartolomeu, including the Bananal, Santa Maria-Torto and Gama tributary systems.

Known only from headwaters of the upper Paraná river basin in the Federal District plus the neighbouring state of Goiás, central Brazil.

Type locality is 'Planaltina, Lagoa Fervedeira, Goiás, Brazil' with additional records existing mostly from the rio São Bartolomeu including the Bananal, Santa Maria-Torto and Gama tributary systems.

At the localities listed in 'Distribution' P. balbus was collected alongside a number of other species including Steindachnerina insculpta, Characidium gomesi, C. xanthopterum, C. zebra, Bryconamericus stramineus, Knodus moenkhausii, Hasemania sp., Astyanax sp., Aspidoras fuscoguttatus, Neoplecostomus corumba, Hypostomus ancistroides, Rhamdia quelen, Rivulus pictus, Phalloceros harpagos, Poecilia reticulata (introduced) and Cichlasoma paranaense.

Psalidodon: from the Ancient Greek ψαλίς (psalís), meaning 'scissors', and ὀδούς (odoús), meaning 'tooth'.

balbus: from the Latin balbus, meaning 'stuttering', in reference to the incomplete lateral line in this species which is described as 'stuttering' in its description.

Moved from Hyphessobrycon balbus to Psalidodon balbus (2024).
